column4: The uprighted wall conceals a treasure for two orphans whose father was righteous, and its repair is mercy rather than a bid for pay; this supplies the preserved value and sound deed behind the wage question in 18:77.
Allah raises the heaven and sets the balance, joining height to measured order immediately before the command to establish weight in 55:9.
The prohibition on transgressing the balance states the failure that 55:9's established just weight prevents.
The usurer rises on Resurrection in a disordered manner after falsely equating usury with trade; commercial value, moral distortion, and bodily standing before judgment meet in one ayah.
Believers are commanded to stand firmly for justice as witnesses even against themselves and their families, directly joining q-w-m posture to equitable judgment.
Believers are commanded to stand for Allah as witnesses in justice and not let hatred bend them from justice, making upright stance an enacted judicial straightness.
The weighing on that Day is truth, and people with heavy scales prosper; 7:9 supplies the deficient opposite.
Those whose scales are light lose themselves because they wronged Allah's signs, joining failed weight, denial, and the adverse verdict.
Those whose scales are heavy are the successful, the positive side of the weighed judgment reversed in 23:103.
Those whose scales are light lose themselves and remain in Hell, carrying deficient weight into the downward final outcome.
Allah sends the Book with truth and the balance, and the same ayah warns that the Hour may be near; revealed standard, assay, and judgment meet directly.
The human being labors toward the Lord and will meet Him, placing every worker and work on a path to the final encounter whose enduring wage appears in 84:25.
People emerge separately to be shown their deeds, supplying the resurrection-and-inspection scene completed by the atom-weight outcomes in 99:7–8.
Spending is pictured as a grain yielding seven hundred grains, the durable multiplied work whose reward is protected from mann and injury in 2:262.
Sincere spending is a high garden that doubles its crop under rain, the productive counterpart to the rain-stripped barren rock of 2:264.
The works of those who deny their Lord are like ashes violently scattered by wind, a specific scene of work retaining no weight or usable value.
Faithless works are a mirage that the thirsty person finds empty, only to find Allah there to settle the account in full; failed product and exact recompense meet.
Allah promises never to waste the work of any worker, male or female, and attaches recompense to costly faithful action, directly preserving both labor and its wage.
Those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer are reformers, and Allah says He does not waste the reward of reformers, joining q-w-m worship, repaired conduct, and preserved pay.
The believer who strives for the hereafter with its proper striving has that striving appreciated, an explicit statement that rightly directed labor retains value.
For the believer who performs righteous works there is no rejection or ingratitude toward the effort, and it is written down, directly opposing the rejected-work image.
Good speech rises and righteous work lifts it or is raised with it, while evil plotting perishes; upright ascent, sound work, and failed work are set together.
Every soul tastes death and receives its wages in full only on Resurrection, joining the end of lifespan to an undiminished final payment.
Allah takes souls at death and during sleep, retains the one decreed to die, and releases the other until a fixed term, making life's ending and measured continuation explicit.
The one who rejects false gods and believes in Allah grasps the firmest handhold, “with no breaking in it,” a concrete unbroken support on the faith side of the section's cut-rope image.
Believers must hold together to Allah's rope and not divide, the direct communal opposite of the severed rope used to explain interrupted reward.
The chiefs of ʿĀd tell Hūd that they think he is a liar; 7:68 answers that charge with his claim to be a trustworthy adviser.
Hūd calls himself “a trustworthy adviser” directly after his people call him a liar, placing reliability and takdhîb's opposite in one exchange.
“If you deny, communities before you denied” extends the fabrication scene of 29:17 and leads into the first-and-final creation proof of 29:19–20.
People are asked whether they see how Allah begins creation and repeats it, the real making that answers the fabricated lie of 29:17.
The command to travel and observe how creation began concludes that Allah will produce the final creation, turning first making into evidence for return.
The question asks whether any alleged partner begins creation and then repeats it; Allah alone does both, separating real creative power from invented partners.
Allah begins creation, repeats it, and then people are returned to Him, compressing making and return into one movement.
Allah originates creation and repeats it, and the supreme attribute belongs to Him, a repeated creation-to-restoration formulation near 30:30's fitrah and upright religion.
People come to Allah alone as He created them the first time, leaving gifts behind while their claimed intercessors and inventions vanish; first creation, return, and failed fabrication meet.
Allah creates the human from a drop, yet the human becomes an open adversary, another direct turn from real creation to the stance of denial.
Creation from dust and a drop is joined to every lengthening or shortening of lifespan being recorded, directly combining human making with measured age.
Allah creates the male and female pair; 53:46 names their drop and 53:47 makes the second bringing-forth His responsibility.
The created pair comes from an emitted drop, supplying the material stage between creation in 53:45 and renewed creation in 53:47.
The second bringing-forth belongs to Allah, completing the first-creation and return sequence of 53:45–46.
Allah creates the human from a mixed drop as a test and equips him with hearing and sight; 76:3 gives the divergent faithful and ungrateful responses.
Allah guides the human to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful, setting two responses before the carefully formed creature of 76:2.
The oath turns to the soul and the One who proportioned it, another direct image of human inner form made fit.
The fashioned soul is shown its corruption and mindfulness, identifying the moral alternatives within the proportioned creation of 91:7.
The one who purifies the fashioned soul succeeds, the soundly maintained side of the form described in 91:7.
The one who corrupts or buries the fashioned soul fails, the moral deformation opposite purification in 91:9.
Allah creates and fashions humanity before commanding the angels to bow to Adam; 7:13 then shows Iblis's proud claim ending in descent and abasement.
Allah asks Iblis why he refused to bow to the human created by His hands and whether he claims to be among the exalted, placing true creation against false self-height.
Iblis is expelled and accursed after claiming superiority over the created human, completing 38:75's reversal from imagined height to descent.
The speaker refuses to seek any judge besides Allah, who sent the Book fully detailed, placing divine adjudication beside a completed, well-determined text.
People do not truly believe until they make the Messenger judge their disputes and submit without inner resistance, making judgment a boundary of faith.
When people are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, a group turns away, directly pairing adjudication with religious refusal.
The believers' response when called for judgment is to hear and obey, the faithful counterpart to the turning away in 24:48.
After the second trumpet blast, the dead are suddenly standing and looking, a direct repeated scene of human beings standing for final judgment.
Every community is seen kneeling and called to its record to be repaid for its works, combining bodily posture, inspected work, and judgment.
Allah's record speaks truth because every work was copied, supplying the reliable account behind the verdict in 45:28.
The coming Event is “lowering, raising,” assigning both vertical reversals to the one judgment the section says lowers and decides.
The Spirit and angels stand in ranks on the Day when none speaks without permission, another concrete courtly standing before the Lord.
The people are told to enter the town, eat freely from it, and enter the gate humbly for forgiveness; 2:59 shows provisioned place reversed by disobedience.
The wrongdoers change the commanded word and receive punishment from heaven, the adverse turn inside the freely provisioned town of 2:58.
Allah confirms that the believers will enter the Sacred Mosque secure and without fear, a direct repeated sacred-place and safety scene.
The Messenger is commanded to worship the Lord of “this town,” who made it sacred, joining place and submission as 30:30 joins creation and religion.
Allah makes earth manageable, commands people to walk its paths and eat His provision, and ends with resurrection to Him; place, livelihood, and rising meet.
Allah spreads earth, anchors it with mountains, and causes everything to grow in due measure, joining ground, fit proportion, and provision.
Allah sets firm mountains, blesses earth, and measures its sustenance, explicitly uniting stable construction, measure, place, and provision.
Blessed rain produces gardens and harvest grain; 50:11 identifies this food as provision and likens the revived land to emergence from death.
Tall palms with layered fruit clusters supply the provisioned growth between blessed rain in 50:9 and resurrection analogy in 50:11.
Good land brings out growth by its Lord's permission, while bad land yields only meagerly, making the ground itself an image of sound and defective yield.
Rain revives a dead land and gives drink to animals and many people, connecting dead soil, life, and distributed provision.
Water produces varied crops that then wither, yellow, and become debris, making earthly provision's measured rise and exhaustion visible.
Worldly life is vegetation that pleases, then yellows and becomes debris, while the afterlife holds punishment or enduring forgiveness, a full passing-versus-remaining comparison.
Worldly life is vegetation mixed with rain that becomes dry fragments scattered by wind, another concrete form of what cannot remain.
Worldly life is rain-grown abundance whose owners think it secured, then Allah's command makes it reaped as though never flourishing, exposing provision's apparent durability.
At the fire Moses is called and told that the fire's surroundings are blessed; this gives the fire encounter its consecrated place before his fear in 27:10.

When Allah manifests to the mountain it is leveled and Moses falls unconscious, then recovers and glorifies Allah; the Mount scene itself stages height, collapse, restored awareness, and judgment before divine presence.
The oath “By the Mount” repeats the sworn object of surah 95 and anchors the Moses-place meeting in another divine oath.
A tree grows from Mount Sinai producing oil and food for eaters, directly joining the Mount, the olive, and provision that surah 95 distributes across its opening oaths.
At death the wrongdoer asks to be returned; 23:100 reveals that the desired return is to perform righteous work and that a barrier prevents it.
The dying person asks to return and do righteous work but is refused and held behind a barrier until resurrection, joining life's cut, return, and belated workmanship.
The guilty stand with heads lowered before their Lord and ask to be returned so they can do righteous work, directly combining descent, judgment, return, and failed labor.
At death a person asks for a short delay in order to give and become righteous, making the ending lifespan the point at which further sound work is cut off.
Allah will not delay a soul once its term arrives, closing the request in 63:10 and fixing the boundary between mortal work and its later wage.
David is told to make full coats of armor, measure their links precisely, and do righteous work, a rare ayah where skilled manufacture, measure, and ṣāliḥ action coincide.
Flood foam and smelting dross vanish as waste while what benefits people remains on earth, joining the moneyworker's furnace to the section's passing-versus-lasting assay.
Even an earth-full of gold would not be accepted as ransom from one who dies faithless, setting the strongest possible market value against divine rejection.
The disbelieving leaders dismiss the message as “a fabrication” (ٱخْتِلَٰقٌ), a direct Quranic use of the kh-l-q family for invented making rather than Allah's real creation.
The question asks whether alleged partners created anything like Allah's creation so that the two creations seemed alike, then declares Allah the Creator of everything.
After identifying the world as Allah's creation, the ayah challenges the audience to show what others created, drawing the boundary between real and claimed making.
Those invoked besides Allah cannot create even a fly, and cannot recover what it takes from them, exposing both failed making and failed recovery.
Whoever submits the face to Allah while doing good grasps the firmest handhold, joining directed religion, sound work, unbroken support, and return of all outcomes to Allah.
Abraham turns his face toward the One who created heaven and earth, upright and free of association, a direct creation-and-directed-religion parallel to 30:30.
Immediately after the fitrah and upright religion of 30:30, people are told to turn back to Allah, be mindful, establish prayer, and avoid association.
The formerly weak and fearful people are sheltered, supported, and provided good things, a direct fear-to-security-and-provision movement.
Allah promises believers who do righteous work succession, establishment of their religion, and replacement of fear with security, joining work, stable religion, and safety.
People exchange Allah's favor for disbelief and settle their people in the abode of ruin; 14:29 names Hell as that destination.
Hell is the evil settlement reached after favor is exchanged for disbelief in 14:28, supplying the downward endpoint of the reversal.
At the descent, earth becomes a temporary settlement and provision; 7:25 then names life, death, and renewed emergence from that ground.
People live and die in earth and will be brought out from it, completing 7:24's descent into a measured earthly stay.
Believers who do righteous works receive multiplied recompense and dwell secure in elevated chambers, combining sound work, wage, height, and security.
People are told to work; Allah, the Messenger, and believers will see the work, and everyone will be returned to the Knower who reports what they did.
Every hardship and step borne in Allah's path is written as a righteous deed, because Allah does not waste the reward of good-doers.
Every contribution and journey is recorded so Allah may reward the best of the people's work, extending 9:120's preserved accounting.
Those who do good receive good, Allah's earth is spacious, and the patient are paid their reward without reckoning, setting divine wage beyond ordinary measure.
Allah raises the Mount over the covenant people and commands them to hold the Book firmly, joining the mountain place to an enacted demand for durable religious adherence.
The mountain is raised above the people like a canopy and they are told to hold firmly to revelation, repeating the Mount-and-firmness scene.
Allah recalls deliverance, appoints the right side of the Mount, and sends down manna and quails as good provision, bringing the Mount, the m-n-n family, safety, and sustenance together.
The rhetorical question asks whether humans thought they were created aimlessly and would not be returned to Allah, directly fusing creation, return, and the surah's interrogative stance.
Allah creates heaven and earth in truth so every soul may be repaid for what it earned without injustice, joining real creation to exact wage.
Heaven and earth are created in truth for a fixed term, yet the disbelievers turn away from the warning, placing measured creation against denial.
People are asked to reflect that Allah created in truth and for a fixed term, while many still deny meeting their Lord.
Allah creates everything and determines it with exact determination, the broad Quranic formulation behind the section's made-fit and measured form.
“Everything We created according to measure” states the relation between creation and exact proportion in its most compressed form.
Whoever trusts Allah finds Him sufficient; Allah brings His purpose to completion and has set a measure for everything, joining reliance, durability, completion, and measure.
Worldly life is diversion and play, while the hereafter is the true life, setting transient appearance against the life that does not fail.
The present life is only temporary enjoyment, while the hereafter is the lasting abode, another explicit statement of what passes and what remains.
No weariness touches the Garden's people and they are never expelled, reversing both the stranded traveler's exhaustion and an interrupted dwelling.
The defrauders are raised “for a tremendous day,” identifying the judicial time between the resurrection question in 83:4 and the standing in 83:6.
Wealth is described as something Allah made qiyām for people and as the source from which they are provided, extending q-w-m from bodily support to economic sustenance.
Joseph's brothers ask why their father does not trust them with Joseph and claim sincere goodwill; 12:17 later exposes the scene's truth-and-trust problem.
The brothers say their father will not believe them even if they are truthful, placing claimed truthfulness against the broken trust requested in 12:11.
People assign partners and invent sons and daughters for Allah even though He created them; 6:101 answers the fabrication with the Creator's absolute making.
The Originator of heaven and earth has no consort and created everything, supplying real creation as the answer to the invented relations of 6:100.
Allah honors Adam's children, carries and provides them, and gives them marked preference, the Quranic positive rank against the human being's possible lowering.
When Moses reaches the fire he is called by name, the transition from the perceived object in 20:10 to the sacred valley in 20:12.
When Joseph's shirt is placed on Jacob's face, he “returns seeing” (ٱرْتَدَّ بَصِيرًا), a restorative bodily reversal within the r-d-d family rather than decline.
After the journey fatigue and lost fish of 18:62–63, Moses and his servant turn back on their tracks, joining the section's exhausted traveler image to literal reversal.
Allah loves those who strive in a row like a solidly joined structure, a nonlexical picture of bodies and workmanship made firm against collapse.
